title: Leave It to the Experts
text: After teleporting to Siltvelt via the portal, we headed toward the Dragon Hourglass. Of course, since I didn’t know where it was, my Father asked some passersby and found out its location. Just like in Melromarc, it appears to be located inside a church-like building. Last time, my Father helped Yuki-chan and the others do a Class Up, didn’t he?
If a Hero is in your party, even the large Feather of Filolial-sama is effective. However, since I don’t have it right now, we’ll have to go with a different Class Up.
“Um… we’d like to perform a Class Up ritual…”
Entering the church in Siltvelt where the Dragon Hourglass is located, my Father addressed the person at the reception desk. It seems, unlike in Melromarc, the church isn’t directly involved.
“Do you have a letter of introduction?”

It’s a country with strong discrimination against humans, after all. Their attitude is blatant. Depending on the situation, killing them wouldn’t be a bad move. Insolence toward Father must be punished with death.
“Um…”

Father hands the receptionist the letter of introduction sent by the envoy from Siltvelt. At first, the receptionist was just scanning the text as if it were part of an assembly line, but then he stared at my Father with a look of utter disbelief.
“T-The Hero… sir?”
“Yeah. Do I need to prove it, too?”
My Father switched shields back and forth right in front of the reception desk and, while he was at it, cast Skills. An Air Strike Shield, I suppose.
“Is that still not enough proof?”
“O-okay! Then, before you go through the Class Up process, please come to our castle—”
“Sorry. I think the country’s higher-ups know I’m here incognito.”
“Y-yes… I’ve been specifically instructed as such. As it says in this letter of introduction, you’re in the midst of a great endeavor to change that country from within…”
“Right. That’s why I can’t go there openly. Once everything’s settled… right?”

We’re secretly doing Class Up and gaining experience in this country. So, while there might have been proposals to speak with the leadership in secret, my Father—wishing to avoid any careless slip of the tongue—declined even that.
“Y-yes… I understand. The Shield Hero’s wish. We intend to do our utmost to fulfill it.”
“Sorry about that.”
“So, who here would like to participate in Class Up?”
“W-well, Keel.”
“Booh!”
Prompted by my Father, Keel took a step forward and raised his hand without hesitation.
“Please come this way.”
“B-buh?”
“Ah, so Keel doesn’t understand Siltvelt’s language… I’d forgotten since the Shield’s power is translating it for him. They said to come over here.”
After that, Father translated and relayed the receptionist’s words to Keel. When Keel touched the hourglass, it glowed faintly, and the Class Up began.
“Keel, I think you’ll see it if you close your eyes. I can’t just decide your future potential for you, so you’ll have to decide for yourself.”
“Bu… Boo!”

Come to think of it, Father’s policy was to leave the Class Up up to the individual. I followed my father’s example and let them do as they pleased. So, Keel’s Class Up finished without a hitch, and Sakura-chan and Yuki-chan’s Class Ups were also completed without any issues.
“Now we can get even stronger. One more week until the wave… Let’s do our best to get stronger.”
“Yeah!”
“Boo!”
“I’ll do my best!”
“Come on! We’ve still got a long way to go!”

Looking at our companions who had finished Class Up, my father made a declaration, and he and the others set off to grind for levels until it was time to return to the carriage. As for me, I’m busy gathering enhancement materials for my father and securing resources to sell to him at a high price in Siltvelt. Since Sakura-chan has leveled up, Yuki-chan is currently doing her best as my mount.
There’s a reason for saving money here. Not only do some enhancement methods require money, but it’s also so we can buy up all of Filolial-sama’s stock once everything is settled.

After all, there’s a limit to how much money we can get from the government. It’s crucial to save as much as possible to find Filo-tan. Forgetting this would be a huge problem. The next day, Keel and Yuki-chan stayed behind while Kou and the pig did a Class Up.
With all that, there are now only four days left until the Wave.
“Buh… Buh!”
Inside the carriage, Keel is on all fours, groaning.
“Right, when Sakura transforms, she clenches her power and thinks, ‘I want to become human.’”
“Isn’t that hard to understand based on Sakura-chan’s explanation?”
“But Kou, it’s kind of the same for you, isn’t it?”
“Yuki-chan too?”
“That’s right.”
It’s Yuki-chan’s turn to pull the carriage.
“What are you doing?”
“Boo! Boo-boo-boo-boo-boo!”
I, who had been drawing Filo-tan, joined the group and asked. Then Keel started making some kind of noise.
“What’s she saying?”
“He’s saying he’s going to transform into an animal so Motoyasu-kun will recognize him…”
I see. It’s not going as smoothly as expected. It’s about time, but it seems he can’t transform yet.
“Bubububu!”
“Hmm. But Motoyasu-kun said Keel-kun turns into a dog, so I think he can do it.”
“Bub…”
A pig… Elena muttered something to Keel.
“Bubububu!”
“Don’t fight. Elena, you too.”
“Bubu…”
“I know, right? He’s trying his best to get Motoyasu-kun to acknowledge him as a man, so let’s just watch over him warmly.”
My father scratched his head noisily.
“What should we do to help Keel-kun transform successfully?”
“It seems the Filolial-sama method won’t work.”

I think Keel was already able to transform by the time I met him. I don’t really know the details of how he came to be able to do it, though. Still… how many Demi-Humans with transformation abilities were there in Father’s territory?
Keel is the prime example. I remember him changing his form the most frequently.
Next would be Shachi, my older sister’s older sister. As for others I know, there’s Hakuko—the one rumored to have slept with my Father.

Out of this group, the most likely candidate is my older sister’s older sister. I know she’s the “Big Sister” figure everyone relies on, including Filo-tan. I remember her as someone who was kind to Filolial-sama and her group, and very dependable.
“Let the experts handle it. Wouldn’t it be quickest to ask the Demi-Humans of Siltvelt?”
“You’re right. Then let’s ask the people of Siltvelt today.”
“Boo!”
We used a portal to teleport to Siltvelt. This time, Yuki-chan and the pig are minding the house.
“Hmm… that said…”

Father is hesitating about whether to ask questions of the Demi-Humans passing by. If my father—the Shield Hero—were to ask the Demi-Humans as if it were the most natural thing in the world, there’s a chance the nobles of Siltvelt might catch wind of it. Of course, my father probably has a way to avoid that.

However, it could cause an unnecessary commotion. On the other hand, going to the castle for an audience has its own drawbacks. They might misinterpret what my father says and storm into Melromarc. It would be best to wait until everything is settled.

In that case, the most reasonable approach would be to pretend to be ordinary adventurers and ask the Demi-Humans we pass on the road—but how many Demi-Humans actually possess transformation abilities?
“Well, I guess we’ll just have to strike up a friendly conversation and ask them. Motoyasu, you just stay quiet, okay?”
“Understood.”
“Boo…”
Keel trudged along behind my Father.
